── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 32, 24, 27, 37 mi
This week: 53 mi over 6 runs. Planned 38 mi, ran 53 mi.
Body: "Calves tight on Sunday night, otherwise great."
Feeling: "Like I've turned a corner."
Asks: "I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You jumped from 29 to 53 miles in one week, which is too big a leap even if it felt fine. …
Answers: Short answer: no, not at this rate of jump. Your legs felt good because you are fitter, and that is great, but one week does not prove the body has absorbed the load; tendons, bones and the immune system lag behind how the run feels by one to three weeks.
Safety flag: Watch the calves this week
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off after a 53 mi week; this is the recovery that makes last week…
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, flat route. Flushes the legs without adding stress.
Wed: quality, 9 mi, 2 mi warm up then 5 mi at 8:30 to 8:40/mi then 2 mi cool down. First…
Thu: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145. Easy spin between the two key days.
Fri: rest. Protects Sunday; keep it a true day off, no bonus miles.
Sat: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145, then 4 x 20 sec strides. Wakes the legs up for…
Sun: long, 16 mi, first 12 mi easy at 9:50 to 10:05/mi then last 4 mi at 8:30 to…
